slides.title: Two ways to take away
slides.text: Subtraction has two faces. It can take away, like eating plums from a bowl. It can also measure the gap between two numbers.

slides.title: Counting up the gap
slides.text: The gap from 287 to 512 is hard to grab in one bite. Count up in friendly hops instead: first to 300, then to 500, then home to 512.

visual.label: Counting up the gap from 287 to 512 in three hops: 13, 200 and 12

focus.cue: The big middle hop: 300 to 500 is 200.
Last hop: 500 to 512 is 12. The gap is 13 + 200 + 12 = 225.

slides.title: Rough first, then hop
slides.text: Rough first: 512 - 287 is about 500 - 300 = 200. Now hop up from 287 and add the hops.

visual.label: The gap drawn as a bar: 512 is 287 plus a gap of 225

focus.cue: Start at 287, the number you count up from.
The rest of the bar is the gap: 225.

slides.title: Stretch: Through the zeros
slides.text: Gaps laugh at tricky zeros. The gap from 398 to 703 hops 398 to 400, then to 700, then to 703. The gap is 305.

visual.label: The gap from 398 to 703 in three hops: 2, 300 and 3

focus.cue: Then 400 to 700 is 300, and 700 to 703 is 3. The gap is 305.

words.means: taking away, or finding the gap between two numbers
the answer to a subtraction: the gap itself
the distance between two numbers on the number line
to start at the smaller number and hop to the bigger one

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sum Racer. It opens on the Subtraction to 100 track, taking-away questions only, and it stays there. Win the race: for this one race, solve every gap by counting up.
